title: Build the Next-Pay Labor Check Premium Blueprint (private preview)
objective:
Build the Premium Blueprint described in agent-specs/ai-payroll-forecasting.json. Read that spec, agents/standards.md, and AGENTS.md first.
Create the public guided demo at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting and the signed-in Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit.
Kit contents: Next-Pay Labor Check Setup Checklist; Next-Pay Labor Check Prompt; Actual-Versus-Projected Prompt; Labor Target and Overtime Rules Worksheet; Loaded Payroll Workbook Template; Schedule Edit Review Checklist; Fictional Sample Schedule Export; Data and Safety Guidance.
Follow every entry in the spec's constraints list.
Do not commit, push, merge, deploy, or publish.
acceptance_criteria: GET /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting without a session renders a page whose h1 is 'Next-Pay Labor Check', with a visible 'Private preview' label.
The guided demo page's HTML contains a robots meta tag whose content includes 'noindex' and 'nofollow'.
The guided demo page shows the fictional data notice text exactly as specified in guided_demo.fictional_data_notice, above the first demo step.

The guided demo is a six-step stepper. It shows the text 'Step N of 6', a 'Next step' button (absent or disabled on step 6), and a 'Previous step' button (absent or disabled on step 1). Each step has a visible heading.

Step 1 shows a table with exactly 2 data rows whose role names are stylist and front_desk, with stylist values 128, 22, and 4 and front_desk values 64, 18, and 0. It also shows '2026-04-06 to 2026-04-19', '9800', '1.20', '40', and '1.5'.

Step 2 shows the exact heading 'NEXT-PAY LABOR CHECK'. It shows stylist formula text '=124*22' and '2728', '=4*33' and '132', and '2860'; front_desk '=64*18' and '1152'; and loaded payroll '=4012*1.20' and '4814.40'.

Step 3 shows calculated labor text '=4814.40/9800' and '49.1%' with text that it is above the 40% target, an overtime flag containing 'stylist' and '4', and the visible text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'OWNER-ENTERED', 'CALCULATED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as words, not as color or icon alone.

Step 4 shows the stylist CONFIRMED line. Activating 'Check facts against the export row' reveals three rows (scheduled_hours 128, hourly_rate 22, overtime_hours_in_schedule 4), each containing the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 shows AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'hours' and 'cannot say whether the $9,800 revenue figure is realistic', variance text '4814.40', '4960', '=4960-4814.40', and '145.60', and the sentence 'Re-check against the actual pay-run total after 2026-04-19.'.

Step 6 contains the exact sentences 'You edit the schedule in your own tool. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not cut hours that break your minimum coverage.' and a link to /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit whose visible text says sign-in is required and the kit is a private preview.
Every role, hour, rate, dollar amount, and percentage in the demo matches the guided_demo.sample_input rows and sample_output exactly.

Neither page contains the text 'checkout', 'buy now', 'purchase', 'Buy Premium', '/month', or 'per month'. The only dollar figures are the fictional schedule and variance amounts (22, 18, 2728, 132, 2860, 1152, 4012, 4814.40, 9800, 4960, 145.60). The only percentages are the fictional target 40% and calculated 49.1%.
Neither page contains an hours-saved figure, a 'you could save' claim, or an ROI or savings-total claim.
The homepage (/) and the site header contain zero links whose href includes '/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting', and /sitemap.xml does not contain '/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting'.
GET /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit without a session redirects to /auth with the query parameter next=/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit.

Next-Pay Labor Check is registered in src/lib/blueprints.ts with id and productSlug 'ai-payroll-forecasting', access 'premium', href '/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit', purchaseHref '/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting', and badge PREMIUM. It is not added to PAID_PRODUCTS and has no Stripe price.

The kit page calls requireUser('/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit') from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement(user.id, 'ai-payroll-forecasting') from src/lib/payments/access.ts. It exports metadata with robots { index: false, follow: false }.

With an authenticated entitled session, the kit page renders h1 'Next-Pay Labor Check Premium Kit' and the exact label text 'Premium · Private preview'. Kit resource and interaction criteria below apply only to this entitled state.

With an authenticated session that has no Next-Pay Labor Check entitlement, the kit page renders h1 'Premium is locked', does not render kit content sections such as #setup-checklist, and does not show a Buy Premium button or a Stripe price.

The kit page shows 8 resource sections with headings matching the kit_contents titles, each with an element id equal to its kit_contents id. A table of contents at the top links to each section with an href of '#<id>'.

The Next-Pay Labor Check Prompt is shown in a <pre> element and contains these strings: 'NEXT-PAY LABOR CHECK', 'CONFIRMED', 'OWNER-ENTERED', 'CALCULATED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', 'RECOMMENDED ACTION', 'loaded payroll', 'Do not invent', 'Do not edit', 'minimum coverage', 'You edit the schedule'.
The Actual-Versus-Projected Prompt is shown in a <pre> element and contains: 'only after', 'actual', 'projected', 'variance', 'Do not invent', 'Do not edit', 'You edit the schedule'.

Each prompt has a 'Copy Prompt' button that writes the exact <pre> text to the clipboard and changes its label to 'Copied'. If the clipboard is unavailable, it shows a visible error telling the person to copy manually.

The Labor Target and Overtime Rules Worksheet has a visible label 'Employer load factor' whose default value is '1.20', a visible label 'Target labor % of revenue' whose default value is '40', a visible label 'Overtime multiplier' whose default value is '1.5', a visible label 'Overtime flag rule' whose default value is 'flag if any role has overtime hours > 0', a visible label 'Minimum coverage by role (optional, one per line)', plus a 'Generate My Labor Check Rules' button.

With the defaults, the generated rules block contains 'Employer load factor: 1.20.', 'Target labor % of revenue: 40.', 'Overtime multiplier: 1.5.', 'Overtime flag rule: flag if any role has overtime hours > 0.', 'Flag only against your target and overtime rule. Do not flag a single busy day.', 'Do not invent rates or savings.', and 'Do not edit shifts or payroll. You edit the schedule in your own tool. The kit changes nothing.' The block has a Copy button.

If the load-factor field is empty or not greater than 0, the worksheet shows the error 'Enter a load factor greater than 0.' and generates no rules block. If the target field is empty or outside 0–100, the worksheet shows the error 'Enter a target labor percentage from 0 to 100.' and generates no rules block.

When 'Minimum coverage by role (optional, one per line)' is empty, the generated rules block contains no 'Minimum coverage' line. When it contains 'stylist: 2 on floor Sat' on one line, the block contains 'Minimum coverage: stylist: 2 on floor Sat.'.

The Loaded Payroll Workbook Template shows the columns role, scheduled_hours, regular_hours, overtime_hours, hourly_rate, regular_pay_formula, overtime_pay_formula, role_subtotal, load_factor, loaded_payroll, revenue_figure, labor_pct_formula, labor_pct, target_pct, flag. Its 'Copy CSV' button writes text whose first line starts with 'role,scheduled_hours' and whose stylist row contains '128', '=124*22', '2728', '=4*33', and '132'.

The Schedule Edit Review Checklist shows 9 checkbox items with visible labels, a progress line 'Checked N of 9', and a 'Reset checklist' button that sets the count back to 0. Progress is not saved beyond the browser session.

The Fictional Sample Schedule Export section is labelled 'Fictional' and its Copy CSV text equals the role,scheduled_hours,hourly_rate,overtime_hours_in_schedule rows and header from guided_demo.sample_input.
The Setup Checklist and the Data and Safety Guidance sections each state that file upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings.
The kit page says that worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in this browser session and are not saved to Atlas.
With an authenticated entitled session, /my-blueprints shows the Next-Pay Labor Check card as Unlocked with an Open Blueprint link to /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit.

With an authenticated session that has no Next-Pay Labor Check entitlement, /my-blueprints shows the Next-Pay Labor Check card as Locked with a Private preview link to /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting and no link to the kit.

With an authenticated session, /my-blueprints still shows the free Daily Inbox Starter Kit with Open Starter Kit pointing at /blueprints/daily-inbox-briefing/starter-kit. AI Collections Assistant entitlement, Buy Premium, and checkout behavior are unchanged. Other Premium Blueprint entitlement and locked or unlocked card behavior are unchanged.

At a 393px-wide viewport, neither page scrolls horizontally (document scrollWidth minus clientWidth is 1px or less) on any demo step or kit section. Tables either wrap or scroll inside their own container.

Every interactive control on both pages can be reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space, and shows a visible focus ring. After 'Next step' or 'Previous step', focus moves to the new step's heading.
Loading both pages produces no unexpected browser console errors or page errors, as judged by the e2e/support/fixtures.ts console filter.

Product implementation files live under app/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/, components/premium/ai-payroll-forecasting/, and src/lib/premium/ai-payroll-forecasting/. The Blueprint registry entry lives in src/lib/blueprints.ts. e2e/ai-payroll-forecasting/authenticated.spec.ts is the protected acceptance test and must not be weakened, skipped, rewritten, or have assertions removed.

Authenticated QA uses the repository's automatic Playwright session refresh. If the session cannot be refreshed, QA stops with AUTH_SESSION_REFRESH_REQUIRED and that failure is not treated as a product defect.
The guided demo at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting renders without sign-in on desktop and a phone-sized viewport, uses only fictional data, and says so.
The kit at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit requires sign-in, is labelled Premium · Private preview, and shows no price, checkout, or purchase claim.
Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header, or sitemap.
Confirmed facts, owner-entered inputs, calculated results, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately, and every external action stays with the person.
The Daily Inbox Briefing, its Starter Kit, and its tests are unchanged.
Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately, and every external action stays with the person.
